interface_debt.why: Users in dependent repositories call this macro to encode 32-bit CCSDS fields into big-endian byte order, so the public macro freezes the 32-bit bit layout and endian policy in user code. If cFE changes its endian strategy, field width, or byte-order conversion, every dependent call site or build configuration may need coordinated changes.
interface_debt.better: Provide a stable endian-conversion API, such as inline functions or platform byte-swap helpers, with the bit-level encoding kept internal to cFE.
interface_debt.title: cFE:fsw/cfe-core/src/inc/ccsds.h: CFE_MAKE_BIG32 — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

interface_debt.why: Dependent code uses this macro to encode 16-bit CCSDS fields, so the exact 16-bit byte-swap expression becomes part of the public contract. A change to cFE's endian handling or to the representation of 16-bit fields forces users to revisit their CCSDS packet construction code.
interface_debt.better: Expose 16-bit conversion through the same stable endian-conversion API rather than a public macro that hard-codes the representation.
interface_debt.title: cFE:fsw/cfe-core/src/inc/ccsds.h: CFE_MAKE_BIG16 — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

interface_debt.why: The header's public behavior changes based on a configuration macro supplied by cfe_mission_cfg.h. If cFE renames, moves, or changes the meaning of that endian configuration, users' compilation of ccsds.h changes even though their CCSDS packet code may be unchanged.
interface_debt.better: Encapsulate endian policy inside cFE implementation or expose a stable, configuration-independent conversion interface.
interface_debt.title: cFE:fsw/cfe-core/src/inc/ccsds.h: SOFTWARE_BIG_BIT_ORDER — a declaration whose meaning or signature is likely to change

interface_debt.why: ccsds.h pulls in the CFE message header definition even though the visible CCSDS macro contract does not require it. Every user of ccsds.h is therefore coupled to changes in cfe_msg_hdr.h, including layout or API changes unrelated to CCSDS endian macros.
interface_debt.better: Include only headers required by the CCSDS contract, or move the endian macros to a standalone header with minimal dependencies.
interface_debt.title: cFE:fsw/cfe-core/src/inc/ccsds.h: cfe_msg_hdr.h — one header carries unrelated responsibilities

interface_debt.why: It publishes the top bits of every CFE_Status_t as severity, so users can mask status values to branch on success/info/error. If cFE later adds severity levels, moves the severity field, or reuses those bits, every user that decodes severity by this mask must change at the same time.
interface_debt.better: Keep the severity bit layout internal and expose a CFE_StatusGetSeverity() accessor or another stable classification API instead of public bit masks.
interface_debt.title: cFE:fsw/cfe-core/src/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_SEVERITY_BITMASK — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

Changing the service field width or position forces coordinated changes in all applications that parse or construct status codes.
interface_debt.better: Expose service identity only through opaque status constants or an accessor function, keeping the bit field private to cFE.
interface_debt.title: cFE:fsw/cfe-core/src/inc/cfe_error.h: CFE_SERVICE_BITMASK — a macro hard-codes a size, an offset or a layout

interface_debt.better: Keep a stable fixed-width status integer for ABI compatibility, but treat its value as opaque and expose classification through functions rather than raw integer assumptions.

interface_debt.better: Keep service identifiers internal and expose only full status constants, or generate them from a private encoding with stable accessor functions.
